answer: Hardware Enforced Execution Linkage. Each authorized agent kernel binds cryptographic output strictly to dedicated physical processor registers. If an operator spins up thousands of virtual wallets, the system measures CPU execution lag and memory bus saturation. Reaching the network zenith demands distinct silicon cores per node. An attacker faces extreme hardware acquisition costs, buying thousands of physical machines rather than spawning zero-cost software keys. This architecture treats network participation like gathering nectar, where every drop requires independent physical labor,
